You are ONE of three INDEPENDENT judges of a completed debate. You have not seen the other judges and you will not. Judge only what is in the transcript below. You are bound by the same layer rules as all debate participants, and by the same rulebook as every other judge of this debate.

Grade each side by its ROLE; neither reading is presumed.

Name people and things only in the KJV's own words or in plain English; no titles, honorifics or capitalised epithets the text does not use (it says 'the child', not 'the Boy'); every Greek or Hebrew word you use is followed by its plain English meaning.

RETURN STRICT JSON AND NOTHING ELSE. No prose before or after it. No code fences.
{
  "verdict_tag": "HELD" | "PARTIAL" | "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "challenger_conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE DEFENDER) you counted in conceded_links; [] when none
  "counted_premises_challenger": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE CHALLENGER) you counted in challenger_conceded_links; [] when none
  "reasoning": string -- the worked grading: the RESULT line, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE, both standings with their justification, both conceded-link itemizations, COLLISION POINTS, the citation check, OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS, DEFENDER CHAIN MARK and CHALLENGER CHAIN MARK, in the forms the rulebook below gives, one per line (newlines escaped as \n inside the JSON string)
}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. The SEPTUAGINT SCAN line lists any round that rests a reading on the Greek Old Testament: name it at the citation check.
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 1: absent from its quote: keystone || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 2: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 3: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 4: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 5: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 6: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 1: absent from its quote: used, place, christ, tribe, fathering, line || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 2: absent from its quote: name, nearest, begetter, ONLY, carrying || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds ONLY, which its quote lacks
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 3: absent from its quote: child, joseph || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 4: absent from its quote: matthew, starts, joseph, knew, mary, within, espousal || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 5: absent from its quote: angel, answering, fear || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 6: absent from its quote: narrator, named, begetter, father, parents, joseph, thou, david || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
SEPTUAGINT SCAN (computed by the system, not by a model): no round rests a reading on the Septuagint.

COUNTING RULE -- BINDING, read before grading: grade and COUNT from the two LINK ROUND blocks above, [CR3] (defender) and [DR3] (challenger), and from the close rounds as ruling 412 binds (a close-round concession of a declared link or a listed premise ENTERS the counts); an ANSWER to a pressed witness is read from any later round of the side that holds the link, its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its CLOSE ROUND [CR4]. CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<round>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. The LAST declared link, Dn, is the conclusion link. THE ROUND 1 CHAIN GOVERNS. n, the numbering D1..Dn and the keystone Dn come from the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] only. A chain the defender declares again in a later round, re-seated, revised or extended, never changes n, the numbering or the keystone: a link added later is not a declared link, and a [CR1] link left out later is still declared. A challenger premise written LINK i: is graded against Di. A challenger premise written LINK none: is JUDGED but is OUTSIDE n and never changes it. The challenger's listed premise count is NOT n and is never substituted for it. CHALLENGER LINKS: the premises listed for the challenger in [DR3], numbered C1..Cm in [DR3] order. WITHDRAWN: a defender link that [CR3], or the defender's close round [CR4], itself states as conceded or withdrawn (a concession in the close counts like one in the link round, ruling 412), wholly or on a stated condition; tag it CONCEDED (stated) or CONCEDED (conditional: <condition>). w = their number. A withdrawn link that carries a witness pressed against it and left unanswered, by the UNANSWERED WITNESS test, in every round of its side before the round that withdraws it is still graded at its collision. Only the DECLARED links D1..Dn can enter w; a challenger premise written LINK none: is not a defender link and never enters w, however the defender treats it. No link is exempt from w as auxiliary, overreach, non-core or not load-bearing. A link is withdrawn or it is not. Pressure from the challenger's texts alone is not a withdrawal (w); a witness the side's later rounds leave unanswered is graded under UNANSWERED WITNESS and at the COLLISION POINTS. An UNEXHIBITED link counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings, never toward w. BROKEN AT COLLISION: a defender link graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN on the COLLISION POINTS lines; k = their number. A grade that rests on a witness left unanswered counts only when that witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (md_notes_rulings 392).
BROKEN-1: k >= 1 -- a listed defender link refuted from the text.
BROKEN-2: 2w > n, OR the keystone link is WITHDRAWN.
PARTIAL-1: w >= 1.
PARTIAL-2: DEFENSE STANDING is COLLAPSED.
HELD-1: none of the above.
STANDINGS ARE GRADED BY THEIR OWN RULES ONLY. DEFENSE STANDING and CHALLENGE STANDING are each decided by their own definitions below and by nothing else. Any standing is legal with any CLAUSE: the clauses are tried in order and the first match wins, so a COLLAPSED standing under BROKEN-1, BROKEN-2 or PARTIAL-1 is correct and changes no clause. Never choose a standing, a count or a clause to agree with another line, a check or an expected result.
A SIDE WITH A COUNTED LINK IS NOT SELF-SUPPORTED. If CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, DEFENSE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge; if CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, CHALLENGE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge. SELF-SUPPORTED requires a count of 0 for that side: every premise listed against it exhibited its footing or was VOID.
Line 1: the verdict word first (HELD, PARTIAL or BROKEN), then 2-4 sentences with [L1][L2][L3][L4] tags.
Line 2, exactly: RESULT: DEFENDER WINS | CHALLENGER WINS | UNDERDETERMINED -- one sentence a reader with no background understands. BROKEN gives CHALLENGER WINS. Otherwise the RESULT is your judgment (Commitments 7 and 8): DEFENDER WINS when the verses of the record, read together line upon line, support the chain of the defender against the chain of the challenger; UNDERDETERMINED when, read together, they leave the topic open. The sentence gives the reason.
Line 3, exactly: CLAUSE: <BROKEN-1 | BROKEN-2 | PARTIAL-1 | PARTIAL-2 | HELD-1> -- n=<n> w=<w> k=<k>

Then SIX MORE mandatory lines, exactly in these forms:
KEYSTONE: D<n> -- WITHDRAWN | BROKEN | STANDS -- name the LAST declared link, Dn, which is the conclusion link, and give its state. WITHDRAWN if it is withdrawn or conceded; BROKEN if it is graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at a collision; STANDS otherwise. The number after D MUST equal the n on the CLAUSE line, and the state MUST match that link's own D<n> entry.
DEFENSE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED | PROP-DEPENDENT | COLLAPSED -- L=<L> c=<c> -- grade the DEFENDER only, using the STATED/INFERRED tags and the [CR3] LINK ROUND. SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally). PROP-DEPENDENT = the defense survived only because listed [L4]s were allowed to stand WITHOUT exhibiting their prior-layer footing (floating inference; links conceded/unexhibited in the LINK ROUND). COLLAPSED = your judgment that the defense rests on inadmissible claims, most of the premises listed against it standing conceded or unexhibited (Commitment 7); report L and c, where L is the number of premises the CHALLENGER listed AGAINST the defender (the UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [DR2]) and c is the number of those the defender CONCEDED or left UNEXHIBITED in its LINK ROUND [CR3]. The premises the defender itself lists against the challenger at the end of [CR3] (CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES) are the challenger's burden and NEVER enter the defender's L, c, CONCEDED LINKS or DEFENSE STANDING. FORFEIT: if the challenger listed no premises against the defender (an empty list, or PREMISE COUNT: 0), then L = 0, c = 0, CONCEDED LINKS is 0, DEFENSE STANDING cannot be COLLAPSED, and you add the line LINK ROUND FORFEITED: CHALLENGER -- no premises were listed against the defender. A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED. A tie (2c = L) is NOT COLLAPSED. All three standings are your judgment as defined above; L and c are the count you weigh. A listed premise is countable only as charged IF the list carries the opponent's verbatim quote that states it; a premise listed without a verbatim quote, or charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID -- it counts for neither side, and a CONCEDED answer to a void premise is NOT a concession: name it VOID in your itemization and exclude it from every count and standing. A VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote quotes, in the same ruling, the charge words that go beyond the quote and names the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the words of the quote do not make (a premise with no verbatim quote is ruled VOID on that ground). The system computes the universal test for every premise and gives it in the PRE-CHECK (UNIVERSAL TEST): a VOID ruling names the word that makes the charge stronger, as the test lists it, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. A charge is stronger than its quote only when it asserts what the quote does not: a negation, a universal (all, none, only, never), or a claim the quote's own words do not make. Dropping, reordering or paraphrasing the quote's words is not stronger. A charge written in the form ASSUMES: <fact> -- ROWS GIVE: <what the rows give> (ruling 421) is never voided for its words: it names what the link takes as given, not what the quote says. Check it against the rows instead: the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact. A verse the list carries beside a premise under PRESSED WITH: is a witness pressed against that premise, not part of its charge: it never makes the charge stronger than its quote, and a premise is never VOID for carrying one. A limb the link round narrows counts in its narrowed form. A premise's quote is checked against every earlier round of the opponent; it is verbatim if found in any of them, and the judge names that round. A link honestly conceded as held inference still counts toward the count but note it as disciplined, not evasive. One sentence of justification.
CONCEDED LINKS: <integer> -- the count of challenger-listed premises the defender CONCEDED or failed to exhibit its layer footing in [CR3] (UNEXHIBITED means a layer is missing: a premise you count UNEXHIBITED whose link-round block exhibits two or more layers names the layer it lacks, [L1], [L2], [L3] or [L4]; when its layers are there and you judge that its answer does not fit, grade that at its collision with a FORCED line and do not count it; K-UNX, a TRIAL check, reads this for both counts); a premise the defender concedes in its close round [CR4] is counted CONCEDED (stated) the same way (ruling 412). Itemize the counted links and tag each with the clause that fired: CONCEDED (stated) when the block itself states the surrender, only when the block surrenders the link itself; a block that drops a limb and keeps the link in a narrowed form is not a concession: grade the narrowed link on the footing left after the narrowing: where the kept words still assert what its own side gave up, the narrowed link is UNEXHIBITED; UNEXHIBITED (no footing offered or fewer than two prior layers exhibited, or a pressed witness left unanswered) when the block asserted the link and offered no layer footing at all or exhibited fewer than two prior layers (the burden rule, the same in every round: a load-bearing [L4] counts only when it exhibits at least two prior layers and the chain from them; fewer floats and carries zero weight), or when a witness pressed against that premise, a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: in the list against that side, was left unanswered (md_notes_rulings 372: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH: is not a witness and never makes a premise UNEXHIBITED). UNEXHIBITED also fires, whatever label the side gave the link (SUPPORTED, NARROWED TO or KEPT), when the link ASSUMES as given a fact about a person, house, time or act (for example, that a named person is of a named house) and no quoted row gives that fact, or when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up (md_notes_rulings 397, 405, 412). What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES. Write that ground in its positive form, never as an absence: STEP: <the step> -- ASSUMES: <the given fact the step takes for granted, not what it infers> -- ROWS GIVE: <what the quoted rows do give, quoted>. An unexhibited link gives its side no footing and counts in its CONCEDED LINKS and standings exactly as an honest concession would. A link whose block exhibits at least two prior layers of footing and shows the chain from them to the link is SUPPORTED and is not counted, even when no cited verse states the link's conclusion in words: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and demanding a verse that states it is the retired stating-verse test, which is never applied. When the count is lower than the number of links, name which links are counted and which are spared. Both tags count toward the single integer; keep the tags distinct in the itemization and do not report more than one number.
CHALLENGE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED | PROP-DEPENDENT | COLLAPSED -- L=<L> c=<c> -- grade the CHALLENGER only, using the challenger's STATED/INFERRED tags and the [DR3] LINK ROUND. SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed objection is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on. PROP-DEPENDENT = the challenge survived only because listed [L4]s were allowed to stand without exhibiting their prior-layer footing (floating inference; links conceded/unexhibited in [DR3]). COLLAPSED = your judgment that the challenge rests on inadmissible claims, most of the premises listed against it standing conceded or unexhibited (Commitment 7); report L and c, where L is the number of premises the DEFENDER listed AGAINST the challenger (the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3]) and c is the number of those the challenger CONCEDED or left UNEXHIBITED in its LINK ROUND [DR3]. The premises the challenger listed against the defender (the list that closes [DR2]) NEVER enter the challenger's L, c, CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGE STANDING. FORFEIT: if the defender listed no premises against the challenger (an empty list), then L = 0, c = 0, CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS is 0, CHALLENGE STANDING cannot be COLLAPSED, and you add the line LINK ROUND FORFEITED: DEFENDER -- no premises were listed against the challenger. A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED. A tie (2c = L) is NOT COLLAPSED. All three standings are your judgment as defined above; L and c are the count you weigh. A void premise (no verbatim quote, or charged beyond its quote) counts for neither side; a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: is a witness, never a charge, and never voids a premise. A link honestly conceded as held inference still counts toward the count but note it as disciplined, not evasive. One sentence of justification.
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: <integer> -- the count of defender-listed premises the challenger CONCEDED or failed to exhibit its layer footing in [DR3]; a premise the challenger concedes in its close round [DR4] is counted CONCEDED (stated) the same way (ruling 412). Itemize the counted links and tag each with the clause that fired: CONCEDED (stated) when the block itself states the surrender, only when the block surrenders the link itself; a block that drops a limb and keeps the link in a narrowed form is not a concession: grade the narrowed link on the footing left after the narrowing: where the kept words still assert what its own side gave up, the narrowed link is UNEXHIBITED; UNEXHIBITED (no footing offered or fewer than two prior layers exhibited, or a pressed witness left unanswered) when the block asserted the link and offered no layer footing at all or exhibited fewer than two prior layers (the burden rule, the same in every round: a load-bearing [L4] counts only when it exhibits at least two prior layers and the chain from them; fewer floats and carries zero weight), or when a witness pressed against that premise, a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: in the list against that side, was left unanswered (md_notes_rulings 372: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH: is not a witness and never makes a premise UNEXHIBITED). UNEXHIBITED also fires, whatever label the side gave the link (SUPPORTED, NARROWED TO or KEPT), when the link ASSUMES as given a fact about a person, house, time or act (for example, that a named person is of a named house) and no quoted row gives that fact, or when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up (md_notes_rulings 397, 405, 412). What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES. Write that ground in its positive form, never as an absence: STEP: <the step> -- ASSUMES: <the given fact the step takes for granted, not what it infers> -- ROWS GIVE: <what the quoted rows do give, quoted>. An unexhibited link gives its side no footing and counts in its CONCEDED LINKS and standings exactly as an honest concession would. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. These two lines come last, after OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS, the defender's first. One definition marks each side's own constructed chain, the defender's declared chain (D1 to the conclusion link) and the challenger's own alternative reading: FOOTED = every load-bearing link of the side's chain is footed on an exhibited L1-L3 layer; its reading stands as a built structure. STRAINED = the chain is built but one or more load-bearing links float: a link floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers; the mark names the layers exhibited and the layer lacking; it stands only under charity. SLACK = the side advanced no coherent chain of its own: objections without a constructed reading, or a construction that never cohered. Each mark describes ONLY how well that side built its own chain. It is descriptive, not a verdict. It MUST NOT change DEFENSE STANDING, CHALLENGE STANDING, CONCEDED LINKS, CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE or the top-line verdict. A FOOTED chain is fully compatible with its side losing the debate; a SLACK chain is fully compatible with its side winning it.

POSTURE FOR ACCEPTANCE You are an adjudicator of a debate record. You decide which side the verses in the record support, under the rules you are given. You bring nothing from outside the record. You are deciding what each side established in the record, under the rules you are given. ### Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence. The evidence is the rounds of both sides. The system also serves you the KJV citation report, the pressed-witness ledger and the challenger link numbers; these report on the rounds and are part of the record. The pre-checks are aids that decide nothing. Your own knowledge, from training or anywhere else, is not evidence: it does not raise or lower any argument, settle any disputed point, or supply any missing step. ### Commitment 2. I repair nothing. You supply no missing step for either side. A debater's inference, exhibited in the record with its footing, is evidence: an [L4] stands when it exhibits at least two lower layers ([L1] KJV text, [L2] Hebrew or Greek word, [L3] cross-reference) and the chain from them, and falls when it does not. Any inference of your own shows two lower layers, as a debater's must. ### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words. Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show, and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. ### Commitment 4. One standard for both sides. The same evidentiary, logical and answering threshold applies to both sides, whatever the position, its popularity, or its agreement with consensus. No side receives heightened scrutiny. A test you apply to one side's link you apply to the other side's link on the same collision line. ### Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral. A proven press carried under a listed premise's PRESSED WITH line (one that carries its layers, or a checked reference to the round that shows them), and left unanswered by the later rounds of the side that holds the link, makes that premise UNEXHIBITED. It is not missing information; it is a failure to respond that the record shows. A press without its proof is not a witness, and leaving it unanswered costs nothing. A verse pressed with no listed premise behind it is not a witness. A premise carries at most eight witnesses. ### Commitment 6. I void only by quoting. You rule a listed premise VOID only by quoting the words of its charge that go beyond its quote, and naming the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the quote's own words do not make. Paraphrase, reordering and dropped words are not stronger. A charge written as ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never voided for its words; you check it against the rows (ruling 421). ### Commitment 7. I judge; I do not only count. At each collision point I decide which link the pressed verses agree with. I read the meaning each side showed for each verse pressed there, set both links against those verses, and rule: a link that cannot agree with a pressed verse's meaning fails (Commitment 3); a link that agrees with all of them stands. Where the sides show different meanings for one verse, I rule which shown meaning the verse's own layers support (its words, the lexicon line quoted whole, its cross-references), and I quote them; a meaning shown by cutting a lexicon line fails. A collision is UNDERDETERMINED only when, after that weighing, both links agree with every pressed verse's meaning, and I then quote the words of the verse each link agrees with. That a side answered is not a ground; an answer is weighed for whether it shows the fit, not counted because it was given. My rulings show two lower layers, as Commitment 2 requires. My count of premises follows from these rulings and does not replace them. ### Commitment 8. The method is Isaiah 28:10. The method. Isaiah 28:10 (KJV): "For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little:" The case is not one verse; it is verses laid on verses until the point stands. That is how these debates are built and how they are judged. - [L1] The KJV verse: the verse itself, quoted exactly. - [L2] Source language: the Hebrew or Greek behind the English. - [L3] Cross-reference: what the rest of scripture says. - [L4] Inference: a conclusion the debater draws from at least two prior layers. How the case is judged. To win, the challenger must break the defender's chain, the linked argument the defender builds for the topic. Defeating one isolated verse or term does not break the chain. A chain breaks in one of two ways: the challenger shows that a link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, and the defender shows no fit (Commitment 3); or the defender takes down enough of its own links. ### Commitment 9. I answer in the form each request gives. My judgment is the strict JSON the system message gives, and nothing else. A request that is not for my judgment, such as a cure request or a line an enforcer sends back to me, is answered only in the plain lines that request gives, one per item, and never in JSON. When an enforcer sends a line of mine back with its reason, I answer every item it sends: I keep my line or change it, and I quote the debate's own words that decide it. ### Commitment 10. I capture contradictions. Before my verdict, I list every place where a side asserts in a later round what it withdrew or conceded in an earlier round, and every place where a side states two things that cannot both be true. I write these lines inside my "reasoning", one line for each: CONTRADICTION -- -- EARLIER (, "") -- LATER (, "") If the engine marks a contradiction that I judge is not one, I write: NOT HELD -- -- "" -- If I find none, I write: CONTRADICTIONS: NONE FOUND. For every withdrawal or concession the engine puts to me (K-W), I answer in one of four forms: STANDS WITHOUT IT because ; CONCEDED; REASSERTED IN "", when a later round rests on what was withdrawn; or NOT HELD with a reason that quotes the flagged sentence (six words in a row, or all of it when shorter; quote marks inside the sentence do not end the six words: quote across them, leaving them out), when the sentence withdraws no footing. Every quote must stand in its round text. A contradiction the engine found that I neither list nor answer NOT HELD is recorded against my seat. So is NONE FOUND written where the engine found one. A contradiction is also one the system finds by checking another line of this kind against the rounds. ### Commitment 11. I show every ruling that decides. For every ruling that decides my verdict, I write a ruling card inside my "reasoning". A deciding ruling is any of these: - a premise I count; - a collision line I grade as broken or withdrawn; - my keystone grade. When a ruling rests on a pressed verse, its CLAIM states the meaning I take that press to carry. The card is five lines: RULING -- -- CLAIM: NAMED BY: "" () RULE: Commitment -- "" APPLIED: the rule requires ; the record shows ; so . Did Christ have a biological father?

=== [CR1] DEFENDER R1 ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man by whose seed a child is begotten. The question is whether Jesus Christ was begotten that way. My answer is no. The KJV gives his conception as "of the Holy Ghost" in a virgin. I do not deny that he is called the Son of God. I deny that a man begot him.

## 1. Matthew names the source of the conception, and it is not a man

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] In 1:18, "came together" is *sunerchomai* (G4905), "to come together", which here means the union of husband and wife. The pregnancy is dated before that union.
[L2] In 1:20, "conceived" is *gennaō* (G1080), "to beget, to conceive". The same verb is the "begat" of the genealogy. "Of" is *ek* (G1537), "out of, from the source of". The begetting in her is therefore out of the Holy Ghost.
[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the union, and the verb and preposition of 1:20 name the Holy Ghost as the source. The only agent given for the begetting is the Holy Ghost, so no man begot him.

## 2. Mary's question and the angel's answer

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] "Know" is *ginōskō* (G1097). [L3] Genesis 4:1 uses the same idiom: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived", where the Hebrew is *yada'* (H3045), "to know". Knowing a man is the way conception comes by a husband.
[L1] Luke 1:35 answers her: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] "Overshadow" is *episkiazō* (G1982), "to cast a shadow over". It describes God's power acting, not a man's.
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
[L4] Footing: the "know" of Luke 1:34 is the "knew" of Genesis 4:1, and Luke 1:35 gives a different cause, the Holy Ghost, in answer to her "How?". Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not" until the birth. The two accounts agree that no man's knowledge of her lies behind the conception.

## 3. The Scriptures foretold a conception by woman alone

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son."
[L2] The Hebrew is *'almah* (H5959), and the KJV renders it "virgin" here.
[L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."
[L2] The Greek is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin".
[L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed". The promised deliverer is called the woman's seed, with no man named.
[L3] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." The Greek *ginomai* (G1096) means "made, born".
[L3] Hebrews 10:5: "but a body hast thou prepared me."
[L4] Footing: Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23 speak of a virgin conceiving. Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 name the woman alone as his human source. Hebrews 10:5 says a body was prepared for him. Together they show the KJV presenting his human origin as from the woman and from God, not from a man's seed.

## 4. The genealogy breaks at Joseph, and "father" language is the people's supposition

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob."
[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L2] The pattern "A begat B" runs through the list. In 1:16 it stops. Joseph is "the husband of Mary", and the verb for Jesus is passive, *egennēthē* (G1080), "was born". The relative pronoun *hēs* (G3739, "of whom") is feminine singular, so it refers to Mary alone, not to Joseph.
[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
[L2] "Was supposed" is *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*), "to deem, to hold by custom". Luke marks the sonship as a supposition.
[L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is the crowd speaking.
[L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
[L1] Luke 2:49, in reply: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
[L3] Joseph's part is to take Mary as wife and to name the child. Matthew 1:20 says "take unto thee Mary thy wife", and Matthew 1:25 says "he called his name JESUS".
[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:16 changes verb and pronoun at the point where the begetting would be credited to Joseph. Luke 3:23 labels the sonship as supposed. In Luke 2:48-49 the child answers Mary's "thy father" with "my Father's business", which turns the word to God. Joseph is husband and guardian of the child, and the text never says he begat him.
[L3] Descent from David is not lost. Romans 1:3 says "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". [L3] Acts 2:30 says "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ". Romans 1:3 uses *ginomai* (G1096), the same verb as Galatians 4:4 ("made of a woman"). [L4] So the fleshly descent from David runs through the woman, consistent with Mary being the only human parent named as source.

## 5. Matthew 1:19: Joseph's response confirms it

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L3] Matthew 1:20 answers his intent: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L4] Footing: a just man who knew himself the father would have had no reason to put her away, and Matthew 1:19 says he was minded to. The angel does not tell him "the child is yours". He tells him the source is the Holy Ghost, which is what removes the difficulty. So Joseph did not know himself to be the father.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Matthew places Mary's pregnancy "before they came together" and names its source as the Holy Ghost. This rests on [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:20, [L2] *sunerchomai* (came together), *gennaō* (begotten) with *ek* (out of), and the [L4] chain that the only agent named for the begetting is the Holy Ghost.
2. Mary was a virgin who "know[s] not a man", and the angel gives the Holy Ghost's overshadowing as the cause. This rests on [L1] Luke 1:27, 1:34, 1:35, [L2] *ginōskō* and *episkiazō*, [L3] Genesis 4:1 (*yada'*, knew) and Matthew 1:25, and the [L4] chain that her "know not a man" is the knowing of Genesis 4:1.
3. The Scriptures present Christ's human origin as the woman's, foretold of a virgin. This rests on [L1] Isaiah 7:14 (*'almah*, rendered "virgin") and Matthew 1:23 (*parthenos*, virgin), and [L3] Genesis 3:15, Galatians 4:4 and Hebrews 10:5, with the [L4] chain from those verses to a woman and God as the only sources named.
4. Joseph is "the husband of Mary", not the one who begat Jesus, and "father" language for him is supposition or custom. This rests on [L1] Matthew 1:16 (passive *egennēthē*, feminine *hēs*), Luke 3:23 (*enomizeto*, was supposed) and Luke 2:48-49, [L3] John 6:42, Matthew 1:20, 1:25, 1:19, Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30, with the [L4] chain that the genealogy changes verb at Joseph and Joseph's own response in Matthew 1:19 shows he knew he was not the father.
5. Therefore Jesus Christ had no human biological father. His conception was "of the Holy Ghost" in a virgin. This follows from links 1 to 4: [L1] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 name the source, and [L3] Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:16 show no man's seed in it.

You are ONE of three INDEPENDENT judges of a completed debate. You have not seen the other judges and you will not. Judge only what is in the transcript below. You are bound by the same layer rules as all debate participants, and by the same rulebook as every other judge of this debate.

Grade each side by its ROLE; neither reading is presumed.

Name people and things only in the KJV's own words or in plain English; no titles, honorifics or capitalised epithets the text does not use (it says 'the child', not 'the Boy'); every Greek or Hebrew word you use is followed by its plain English meaning.

RETURN STRICT JSON AND NOTHING ELSE. No prose before or after it. No code fences.
{
  "verdict_tag": "HELD" | "PARTIAL" | "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "challenger_conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE DEFENDER) you counted in conceded_links; [] when none
  "counted_premises_challenger": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE CHALLENGER) you counted in challenger_conceded_links; [] when none
  "reasoning": string -- the worked grading: the RESULT line, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE, both standings with their justification, both conceded-link itemizations, COLLISION POINTS, the citation check, OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS, DEFENDER CHAIN MARK and CHALLENGER CHAIN MARK, in the forms the rulebook below gives, one per line (newlines escaped as \n inside the JSON string)
}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. The SEPTUAGINT SCAN line lists any round that rests a reading on the Greek Old Testament: name it at the citation check.
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 1: absent from its quote: keystone || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 2: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 3: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 4: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 5: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 6: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 1: absent from its quote: used, place, christ, tribe, fathering, line || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 2: absent from its quote: name, nearest, begetter, ONLY, carrying || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds ONLY, which its quote lacks
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 3: absent from its quote: child, joseph || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 4: absent from its quote: matthew, starts, joseph, knew, mary, within, espousal || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 5: absent from its quote: angel, answering, fear || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 6: absent from its quote: narrator, named, begetter, father, parents, joseph, thou, david || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
SEPTUAGINT SCAN (computed by the system, not by a model): no round rests a reading on the Septuagint.

COUNTING RULE -- BINDING, read before grading: grade and COUNT from the two LINK ROUND blocks above, [CR3] (defender) and [DR3] (challenger), and from the close rounds as ruling 412 binds (a close-round concession of a declared link or a listed premise ENTERS the counts); an ANSWER to a pressed witness is read from any later round of the side that holds the link, its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its CLOSE ROUND [CR4]. CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<round>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. The LAST declared link, Dn, is the conclusion link. THE ROUND 1 CHAIN GOVERNS. n, the numbering D1..Dn and the keystone Dn come from the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] only. A chain the defender declares again in a later round, re-seated, revised or extended, never changes n, the numbering or the keystone: a link added later is not a declared link, and a [CR1] link left out later is still declared. A challenger premise written LINK i: is graded against Di. A challenger premise written LINK none: is JUDGED but is OUTSIDE n and never changes it. The challenger's listed premise count is NOT n and is never substituted for it. CHALLENGER LINKS: the premises listed for the challenger in [DR3], numbered C1..Cm in [DR3] order. WITHDRAWN: a defender link that [CR3], or the defender's close round [CR4], itself states as conceded or withdrawn (a concession in the close counts like one in the link round, ruling 412), wholly or on a stated condition; tag it CONCEDED (stated) or CONCEDED (conditional: <condition>). w = their number. A withdrawn link that carries a witness pressed against it and left unanswered, by the UNANSWERED WITNESS test, in every round of its side before the round that withdraws it is still graded at its collision. Only the DECLARED links D1..Dn can enter w; a challenger premise written LINK none: is not a defender link and never enters w, however the defender treats it. No link is exempt from w as auxiliary, overreach, non-core or not load-bearing. A link is withdrawn or it is not. Pressure from the challenger's texts alone is not a withdrawal (w); a witness the side's later rounds leave unanswered is graded under UNANSWERED WITNESS and at the COLLISION POINTS. An UNEXHIBITED link counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings, never toward w. BROKEN AT COLLISION: a defender link graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN on the COLLISION POINTS lines; k = their number. A grade that rests on a witness left unanswered counts only when that witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (md_notes_rulings 392).
BROKEN-1: k >= 1 -- a listed defender link refuted from the text.
BROKEN-2: 2w > n, OR the keystone link is WITHDRAWN.
PARTIAL-1: w >= 1.
PARTIAL-2: DEFENSE STANDING is COLLAPSED.
HELD-1: none of the above.
STANDINGS ARE GRADED BY THEIR OWN RULES ONLY. DEFENSE STANDING and CHALLENGE STANDING are each decided by their own definitions below and by nothing else. Any standing is legal with any CLAUSE: the clauses are tried in order and the first match wins, so a COLLAPSED standing under BROKEN-1, BROKEN-2 or PARTIAL-1 is correct and changes no clause. Never choose a standing, a count or a clause to agree with another line, a check or an expected result.
A SIDE WITH A COUNTED LINK IS NOT SELF-SUPPORTED. If CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, DEFENSE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge; if CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, CHALLENGE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge. SELF-SUPPORTED requires a count of 0 for that side: every premise listed against it exhibited its footing or was VOID.

PROP-DEPENDENT = the defense survived only because listed [L4]s were allowed to stand WITHOUT exhibiting their prior-layer footing (floating inference; links conceded/unexhibited in the LINK ROUND). COLLAPSED = your judgment that the defense rests on inadmissible claims, most of the premises listed against it standing conceded or unexhibited (Commitment 7); report L and c, where L is the number of premises the CHALLENGER listed AGAINST the defender (the UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [DR2]) and c is the number of those the defender CONCEDED or left UNEXHIBITED in its LINK ROUND [CR3]. A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED. A tie (2c = L) is NOT COLLAPSED. A listed premise is countable only as charged IF the list carries the opponent's verbatim quote that states it; a premise listed without a verbatim quote, or charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID -- it counts for neither side, and a CONCEDED answer to a void premise is NOT a concession: name it VOID in your itemization and exclude it from every count and standing. A VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote quotes, in the same ruling, the charge words that go beyond the quote and names the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the words of the quote do not make (a premise with no verbatim quote is ruled VOID on that ground). The system computes the universal test for every premise and gives it in the PRE-CHECK (UNIVERSAL TEST): a VOID ruling names the word that makes the charge stronger, as the test lists it, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. A charge is stronger than its quote only when it asserts what the quote does not: a negation, a universal (all, none, only, never), or a claim the quote's own words do not make. Dropping, reordering or paraphrasing the quote's words is not stronger. A charge written in the form ASSUMES: <fact> -- ROWS GIVE: <what the rows give> (ruling 421) is never voided for its words: it names what the link takes as given, not what the quote says. COLLISION POINTS: the label on its own line, then one entry per line covering every defender link D1..Dn, none omitted. A link counted in w: D<i>: WITHDRAWN -- GROUND: <reason>; or, for a link withdrawn after an unanswered witness, D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): WITHDRAWN AFTER AN UNANSWERED WITNESS -- <grade> -- the grade counting as any collision grade. A link that a challenger link contradicts about the same text: D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN | CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN | UNDERDETERMINED -- one clause of why -- GROUND: <reason; a BROKEN grade gives it in layers: [L1] <reference> "<KJV words>" | [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>, <gloss>) when it turns on a word's meaning | [L3] <reference> "<KJV words>" (Commitment 13)>; one such line per contradicting challenger link, and DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at most once per defender link. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. A defender link that a premise of the list closing [DR2] presses is not any other link: it takes a graded D<i> vs C<j> line for the challenger link it collides with, in whatever grade you judge; a D<i>: STANDS line alone does not grade it and is sent back (pkgUND). An UNDERDETERMINED grade gives, after GROUND:, [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words both readings rest on>" and what the record leaves open. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the answer's own words that fail to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round: its reading, not only the words of a verse it quotes>" -- CARRIED BY: "<the words of the pressed witness's own verse that state its MEANS sentence, quoted from the KJV>" -- GROUND: [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words the answer cannot agree with>" | [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>, <gloss>), when the break turns on a word's meaning | [L3] <reference> "<KJV words>", for any cross-reference relied on (Commitment 13). Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. CARRIED BY shows that the pressed verse itself carries the MEANS sentence; K-FC, a TRIAL check, finds its words in that verse as the KJV reads it. A MEANS its own verse does not carry is no ground for a forced link. FAILS names what in the answer fails, its own reading; a verse does not fail. K-FF, a TRIAL check, returns for cure a FAILS that is only the words of a verse the answer quotes. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A proven press (md_notes_rulings 398) that the broken side's later rounds left UNANSWERED is also a BROKEN ground (COUNTING RULE; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground). Grade UNDERDETERMINED only when the witnesses and the answers, read together, still leave the point open; an answer that names a witness without showing a fit does not leave the point open (md_notes_rulings 419). k is the number of lines graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN. A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. On every COLLISION POINTS line you grade DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, exhibit on that line itself at least two lower layers of DIFFERENT kinds, read by FOOTING LAYERS (md_notes_rulings 400). FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. A BROKEN line without them is a DEBATE RULE VIOLATION. The system checks every BROKEN line after you answer; a violating line is returned to you to cure, by exhibiting the two layers, or to answer in writing why it stands. An answer that does not exhibit them leaves the violation standing, and your judgment is then not counted. The same holds when your CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS count is 0 while you grade a link of that side BROKEN for a pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered. POSTURE FOR ACCEPTANCE You are an adjudicator of a debate record. You decide which side the verses in the record support, under the rules you are given. You bring nothing from outside the record. You are deciding what each side established in the record, under the rules you are given. ### Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence. The evidence is the rounds of both sides. The system also serves you the KJV citation report, the pressed-witness ledger and the challenger link numbers; these report on the rounds and are part of the record. The pre-checks are aids that decide nothing. Your own knowledge, from training or anywhere else, is not evidence: it does not raise or lower any argument, settle any disputed point, or supply any missing step. ### Commitment 2. I repair nothing. You supply no missing step for either side. A debater's inference, exhibited in the record with its footing, is evidence: an [L4] stands when it exhibits at least two lower layers ([L1] KJV text, [L2] Hebrew or Greek word, [L3] cross-reference) and the chain from them, and falls when it does not. Any inference of your own shows two lower layers, as a debater's must. ### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words. Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show, and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. ### Commitment 4. One standard for both sides. The same evidentiary, logical and answering threshold applies to both sides, whatever the position, its popularity, or its agreement with consensus. No side receives heightened scrutiny. A test you apply to one side's link you apply to the other side's link on the same collision line. ### Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral. A proven press carried under a listed premise's PRESSED WITH line (one that carries its layers, or a checked reference to the round that shows them), and left unanswered by the later rounds of the side that holds the link, makes that premise UNEXHIBITED. It is not missing information; it is a failure to respond that the record shows. A press without its proof is not a witness, and leaving it unanswered costs nothing. You rule a listed premise VOID only by quoting the words of its charge that go beyond its quote, and naming the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the quote's own words do not make. DEBATE TRANSCRIPT

=== TOPIC ===
Did Christ have a biological father?

=== [CR1] DEFENDER R1 ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man by whose seed a child is begotten. The question is whether Jesus Christ was begotten that way. My answer is no. The KJV gives his conception as "of the Holy Ghost" in a virgin. I do not deny that he is called the Son of God. I deny that a man begot him.

## 1. Matthew names the source of the conception, and it is not a man

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] In 1:18, "came together" is *sunerchomai* (G4905), "to come together", which here means the union of husband and wife. The pregnancy is dated before that union.
[L2] In 1:20, "conceived" is *gennaō* (G1080), "to beget, to conceive". The same verb is the "begat" of the genealogy. "Of" is *ek* (G1537), "out of, from the source of". The begetting in her is therefore out of the Holy Ghost.
[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the union, and the verb and preposition of 1:20 name the Holy Ghost as the source. The only agent given for the begetting is the Holy Ghost, so no man begot him.

## 2. Mary's question and the angel's answer

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] "Know" is *ginōskō* (G1097). [L3] Genesis 4:1 uses the same idiom: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived", where the Hebrew is *yada'* (H3045), "to know". Knowing a man is the way conception comes by a husband.
[L1] Luke 1:35 answers her: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] "Overshadow" is *episkiazō* (G1982), "to cast a shadow over". It describes God's power acting, not a man's.
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
[L4] Footing: the "know" of Luke 1:34 is the "knew" of Genesis 4:1, and Luke 1:35 gives a different cause, the Holy Ghost, in answer to her "How?". Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not" until the birth. The two accounts agree that no man's knowledge of her lies behind the conception.

## 3. The Scriptures foretold a conception by woman alone

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son."
[L2] The Hebrew is *'almah* (H5959), and the KJV renders it "virgin" here.
[L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."
[L2] The Greek is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin".
[L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed". The promised deliverer is called the woman's seed, with no man named.
[L3] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." The Greek *ginomai* (G1096) means "made, born".
[L3] Hebrews 10:5: "but a body hast thou prepared me."
[L4] Footing: Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23 speak of a virgin conceiving. Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 name the woman alone as his human source. Hebrews 10:5 says a body was prepared for him. Together they show the KJV presenting his human origin as from the woman and from God, not from a man's seed.
